title: White card vs high risk work licence: what is the difference?
seoTitle: White card vs high risk work licence
description: A white card is general construction induction for anyone on a building site; a high risk work licence authorizes one of 29 classes of plant work and expires.
shortAnswer: In Australia, a white card (general construction induction training card) shows a person has completed basic safety induction and is required for anyone who carries out construction work. A high risk work licence authorizes a person to perform one specific class of high risk work, such as operating a forklift or crane, scaffolding or rigging. The white card has no expiry date but lapses after two years without construction work; a high risk work licence expires after five years.
keyTakeaways: The white card is general and entry level: one card, one course, for every construction worker. A high risk work licence is specific: each of the 29 classes in Schedule 3 of the model WHS Regulations needs its own licence.
White card training is delivered by a Registered Training Organisation; high risk work licence applicants must be at least 18, hold the Schedule 4 qualification and be assessed.
A white card carries no expiry date, but a business must retrain a worker whose training is more than two years old if they have not done construction work in the preceding two years.
A high risk work licence expires five years after it is granted, and renewal requires a declaration that competency has been maintained.
Victoria runs both credentials under its own Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017, with 30 licence classes and a face to face induction course.

sections.heading: What is the core difference between a white card and a high risk work licence?

blocks.text: The core difference is breadth versus authorization. A white card proves general awareness of construction site hazards and is a precondition for being on a construction job at all. A high risk work licence authorizes the holder to perform one defined task class that the law reserves for licensed people, and doing that work without the licence is an offense.

Under Part 6.5 of the [model Work Health and Safety Regulations](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-work-health-and-safety-regulations), regulation 316 requires a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU) to ensure that general construction induction training is provided to a worker who has not completed it, or who completed it more than two years earlier and has not carried out construction work in the preceding two years. Regulation 317 requires the worker to hold a general construction induction training card. Safe Work Australia [says white cards are recognized Australia wide](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/safety-topic/industry-and-business/construction/working-construction-site). Detail is on [general construction induction and the white card](/regulations/general-construction-induction-white-card).

Under Part 4.5 of the [same Regulations](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-12/model-whs-regulations-5_december_2025.pdf), regulation 81 prohibits a person from carrying out a class of high risk work without the relevant licence. Schedule 3 lists 29 classes, covering scaffolding, dogging and rigging, cranes and hoists, reach stackers, forklifts, boilers, steam turbines and reciprocating steam engines. See [high risk work licence requirements](/regulations/high-risk-work-licence-requirements).

sections.heading: When does a worker need both?

blocks.text: A worker needs both whenever high risk work is done as part of construction work. The licence authorizes the task; the white card authorizes presence on the construction job. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither replaces site specific induction.

A forklift operator moving materials on a building site, for example, needs the forklift class licence and a white card. A forklift operator in a warehouse needs only the licence, because warehouse work is not construction work. A laborer on a building site who operates no licensed plant needs only the white card.

Both credentials sit below the site's own duties. Safe Work Australia's [Construction work Code of Practice](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-code-practice-construction-work) describes workplace specific induction topics in section 6.2, and high risk construction work also requires a safe work method statement under Part 6.3. Competence to operate a particular machine on a particular site still needs to be confirmed by the business, which is where [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) comes in.

blocks.title: Practical consequence
blocks.text: A licence or card proves the person passed a nationally recognized course or assessment at some point. It does not show they can do the task safely on this site with this equipment today. Record the credential check and the site level competency check separately.

sections.heading: Which rules apply in your state or territory?

blocks.text: Every jurisdiction except Victoria has adopted the model WHS laws, so the model Regulations described here apply in New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, the Australian Capital Territory, the Northern Territory and for Commonwealth workplaces, administered by each regulator. Victoria has its own regime.

items: **Model WHS jurisdictions:** white card under regulations 316 to 320 and licences under Part 4.5. State regulators issue the credentials; SafeWork NSW, for example, states that white cards are void after two consecutive years without construction work and that licence assessment is done by an accredited assessor.

**Victoria:** the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017 require a current construction induction card, which lapses after a consecutive two year period without construction work. WorkSafe Victoria requires the induction course to be face to face, not online, and lists 30 licence classes, including non slewing telehandlers over 3 tonnes. See [Victoria's construction induction and high risk work regime](/regulations/victoria-construction-induction-and-hrw-regime).
**Interstate workers:** the model Regulations recognize cards issued under a corresponding WHS law (regulation 318), and Victoria's regulations recognize interstate evidence.
**Workers from overseas:** the course must be delivered in Australia by a Registered Training Organisation for a card to count under the model definition.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each role and task to the credential rules that apply in its jurisdiction, with provenance to the regulation, and separates credential evidence from site level competency evidence. When a regulator changes a class or a lapse rule, the affected roles and records are identified from those links.

faqs.a: The card itself has no expiry date under the model Regulations, which list its contents without one. However, a PCBU must provide induction training again to a worker who completed it more than two years earlier and has not carried out construction work in the preceding two years. Victoria's regulations say the card lapses after a consecutive two year period without construction work.

faqs.q: Can white card training be done online?
faqs.a: It depends on the jurisdiction. WorkSafe Victoria states that construction induction training must be delivered face to face and cannot be done online, with a minimum of six hours. Other regulators set their own delivery rules for the course, so check the regulator in the state where the card will be issued.

faqs.q: Is a licence needed to operate an excavator or scissor lift?
faqs.a: Not under the high risk work licence classes. WorkSafe Victoria states that no high risk work licence is required for excavators or scissor lifts, and neither appears among the Schedule 3 classes of the model Regulations. The business must still ensure operators are trained and competent under its general duty.

faqs.q: Who checks a worker's high risk work licence?
faqs.a: The business directing the work. Regulation 85 of the model Regulations requires a PCBU to see written evidence that a worker holds the relevant licence before directing or allowing the work, and to keep a record of that evidence for at least one year after the work ends.
